# keelyard documentation (full text)

Source: https://github.com/akobirjontulqinovfuture/keelyard · Docs: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/

# keelyard

<p class="lede">Your coding agent has to show its work before it can say "done". Every edit is snapshotted, so any
step can be undone. Logs are trimmed before they eat the context window. keelyard works with Claude Code, Codex
and OpenCode.</p>

![keelyard in a terminal](img/hero.gif)

```bash
pipx install keelyard
cd your-project
keelyard init
```

That is the whole setup. `keelyard init` finds the agents on your machine and wires each one: hooks, the MCP
server, a short guide in `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, and a skill plus slash commands for Claude Code.
After that it takes a first snapshot.

## The pieces

| | What you get |
|---|---|
| [Proof gate](guide/proof.md) | The agent can't finish until there is a checklist, evidence for every item, and a passing test run after its last edit. You get a one-file HTML report. |
| [Rewind](guide/rewind.md) | A snapshot after every edit, in a separate git repo. Undo any step and fork from any step. |
| [Smaller context](guide/context.md) | Output filters that keep every failure, deduplicated reads, `project_map` / `outline` / `find_symbol`. |
| [Memory and usage](guide/memory.md) | Search across past sessions from all three agents. Tokens and cost from local logs. |
| [Swarm](guide/swarm.md) | Bulk reading and drafting on a cheap model, with every citation checked. |
| [Arena](guide/arena.md) | One task, several agents and models: pass rate, time and tokens side by side. |

## What it is not

keelyard is not a proxy and does not read your API traffic. It does not change your `.git`, and it does not send
anything over the network unless you configure a helper model for `swarm`. Every number in these docs was
measured. See [Benchmarks](BENCHMARKS.md), including the results that did not go our way.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/quickstart/

# Quickstart

## Install

keelyard needs Python 3.11 or newer and git.

```bash
pipx install keelyard
```

`pip install` works too. Agents call `keelyard` by name, so it has to be on `PATH`. `keelyard doctor`
checks that.

## Set up a project

```bash
cd your-project
keelyard init
```

![keelyard init](img/cli-init.png)

- With no flags, every agent found on this machine is wired. To pick agents, use `--agent claude`
  (you can repeat the flag). To see what would change without changing anything, use `--dry-run`.
- **Codex** needs two extra steps. Paste the printed `[mcp_servers.keelyard]` block into
  `~/.codex/config.toml`, then run `/hooks` once inside Codex to trust the hooks.
- Running `init` again is safe. It updates keelyard's own entries and leaves yours alone.

## Check it

```bash
keelyard doctor     # installation and wiring; exits 3 if something is broken
keelyard selftest   # a scripted agent does a full task through MCP and hooks, in a temp folder
```

![keelyard doctor](img/cli-doctor.png)

## Use your agent

Work as usual. While the agent works:

```bash
keelyard status          # snapshots, proof checklist, what is still open
keelyard rewind list     # every step, newest last
keelyard rewind to 7     # put files back as they were after step 7
keelyard proof report    # the HTML report for this session
```

![keelyard status](img/cli-status.png)

## Remove it

```bash
keelyard uninstall claude    # removes only keelyard's entries
rm -rf .keelyard             # snapshots, proof bundles, caches
```

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/codex/

# keelyard + Codex in 2 minutes

keelyard plugs into the [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) through three things Codex already supports:
lifecycle **hooks** (`.codex/hooks.json`), an **MCP server**, and **AGENTS.md**. You keep using Codex as usual.

**Checked with Codex CLI 0.165.0** (Oct 28, 2026) by [`scripts/codex_e2e.py`](https://github.com/akobirjontulqinovfuture/keelyard/blob/main/scripts/codex_e2e.py),
which runs the real Codex binary against a local scripted model, so it needs no OpenAI key. CI runs it on every push.

## 1. Install

```bash
pipx install keelyard        # or: pip install keelyard
npm i -g @openai/codex       # if you don't have Codex yet
```

## 2. Wire up your project

```bash
cd your-project
keelyard init --agent codex --codex-project-mcp
keelyard doctor
```

This writes:

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `.codex/hooks.json` | `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop` → `keelyard hook codex <event>` |
| `.codex/config.toml` | `[mcp_servers.keelyard]` (only with `--codex-project-mcp`) |
| `AGENTS.md` | a short block between `<!-- keelyard:start -->` and `<!-- keelyard:end -->` |
| `.keelyard/` | config and snapshots (a separate git dir; your `.git` is never touched) |

Originals are kept, and `keelyard uninstall codex` restores them byte for byte.

Prefer the MCP server for every project? Put it in `~/.codex/config.toml` instead (or run
`codex mcp add keelyard -- keelyard mcp`):

```toml
[mcp_servers.keelyard]
command = "keelyard"
args = ["mcp"]
```

`codex mcp list` should now show `keelyard  …  enabled`.

The AGENTS.md block keelyard adds (lean preset) is three lines:

```markdown
## keelyard

Every edit is snapshotted (undo: `keelyard rewind list`, `keelyard rewind to N`). Your shell test runs are the proof:
run the project's tests after your last edit before you finish.
Be terse: no preamble or recap. Keep code exact.
```

## 3. Trust the hooks once

Codex only runs hooks you have reviewed. Start `codex` in the project, type **`/hooks`**, and trust the five keelyard
hooks. Codex also needs the project itself to be trusted to load `.codex/` (it asks the first time).
For one-off automation where you vetted the hooks yourself, `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` skips the
review for that run.

## 4. What you see

- **Session start:** a brief with the project's test command and a baseline test result.
- **Every edit** (`apply_patch` or a shell command that changes files) is snapshotted:
  `keelyard rewind list`, `keelyard rewind to 3`.
- **When Codex says "done" with red or unrun tests,** the `Stop` hook sends it back with what is missing:

  ```text
  keelyard proof gate: you changed files but have not proven the work yet.
  - No test run after the last edit (proof_run_tests phase='after', or `keelyard proof test after`).
  Run the project's tests in your shell (that counts as proof), or use the keelyard proof tools, then finish.
  ```

  A test run in Codex's own shell counts as proof; Codex does not need to call keelyard. The gate gives up after
  three blocks so a session can never loop forever.
- **Afterwards:** `keelyard status` shows `proof proven`, the evidence and the timeline.

## Verify it yourself

```bash
git clone https://github.com/akobirjontulqinovfuture/keelyard && cd keelyard
pip install -e . pytest && npm i -g @openai/codex
python scripts/codex_e2e.py
```

Expected output: 11 `PASS` lines (hooks file, AGENTS.md, `codex mcp list`, MCP tools and AGENTS.md reaching the
model, each hook event firing, the gate blocking a red "Done.", the gate opening after a passing run,
`keelyard status` proven, rewind restoring the broken edit).

## Known limits with Codex

- **Output filtering does not apply.** Codex hooks can't replace a shell result yet, so keelyard's log compression
  works through the MCP `run_compact` tool only, not on Codex's own shell calls.
- **No lean switch for Codex tools.** The lean preset can turn some Claude Code / OpenCode tools off; Codex has no
  config for that, so on Codex lean means the shorter brief and AGENTS.md block.
- **Token savings on Codex are not measured yet.** The e2e check uses a scripted model, which proves the wiring,
  not savings. Real-model numbers are on the [roadmap](https://github.com/akobirjontulqinovfuture/keelyard/blob/main/ROADMAP.md).
- Codex's own sandbox rejects some commands (for example `rm -rf`) before keelyard's `PreToolUse` sees them.

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/claude-code/

# keelyard + Claude Code in 2 minutes

keelyard plugs into [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) through three things Claude Code
already supports: lifecycle **hooks** (`.claude/settings.json`), an **MCP server** (`.mcp.json`), and **CLAUDE.md**.
You keep using Claude Code as usual.

**Checked with Claude Code 2.1.197** (Oct 29, 2026) by [`scripts/claude_e2e.py`](https://github.com/akobirjontulqinovfuture/keelyard/blob/main/scripts/claude_e2e.py):
the real `claude` binary in `-p` mode against a local scripted model (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`), so no Anthropic key is
used. CI runs it on every push and weekly.

## 1. Install

```bash
pipx install keelyard                       # or: pip install keelyard
npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code          # if you don't have Claude Code yet
```

## 2. Wire up your project

```bash
cd your-project
keelyard init --agent claude
keelyard doctor
```

This writes:

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `.claude/settings.json` | hooks `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreCompact`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop` → `keelyard hook claude <event>`; lean preset also sets `env` (capped tool output, no extra model calls) |
| `.mcp.json` | `mcpServers.keelyard` → `keelyard mcp` (project scope) |
| `CLAUDE.md` | a short block between `<!-- keelyard:start -->` and `<!-- keelyard:end -->` |
| `.claude/skills/keelyard/` | a keelyard skill |
| `.claude/commands/keelyard/` | `/keelyard:prove`, `review`, `status`, `debug`, `plan`, `undo` |
| `.keelyard/` | config and snapshots (a separate git dir; your `.git` is never touched) |

Originals are kept, and `keelyard uninstall claude` restores them. For every project at once, use
`keelyard init --global` (writes `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.claude.json` and `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`).

## 3. Approve the MCP server once

Claude Code asks before it starts servers from a project's `.mcp.json`. Until then:

```text
$ claude mcp list
keelyard: keelyard mcp - ⏸ Pending approval (run `claude` to approve)
```

Start `claude` in the project and accept the keelyard server. Prefer it for every project? Run
`claude mcp add --scope user keelyard -- keelyard mcp` instead. The hooks need no approval.

## 4. What you see

- **Session start:** a brief with the project's test command and a baseline test result.
- **Every edit** (Edit/Write or a Bash command that changes files) is snapshotted:
  `keelyard rewind list`, `keelyard rewind to 3`.
- **When Claude says "done" with red or unrun tests,** the `Stop` hook sends it back:

  ```text
  Stop hook feedback:
  keelyard proof gate: you changed files but have not proven the work yet.
  ```

  A test run in Claude's own Bash tool counts as proof. The gate gives up after three blocks, so it never loops.
- **Tools:** `mcp__keelyard__proof_check`, `proof_run_tests`, `memory_search`, `find_symbol`, … are available to the model.
- **Afterwards:** `keelyard status` shows `proof proven`, the evidence and the timeline.

## What was checked (Claude Code 2.1.197)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `claude mcp list` shows keelyard from `.mcp.json` | yes (pending approval until accepted) |
| keelyard MCP tools and the CLAUDE.md block reach the model | yes |
| hooks fire: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop | yes (`PreCompact` needs a long session) |
| gate blocks a "Done." after a breaking edit with no test run | yes |
| gate opens after a passing `pytest` in Claude's Bash | yes, `keelyard status` → proven |
| `keelyard rewind to 2` brings back the broken edit | yes |

Not checked: token savings with a real Claude model, and `PreCompact` (needs a long session).

## Verify it yourself

```bash
git clone https://github.com/akobirjontulqinovfuture/keelyard && cd keelyard
pip install -e . pytest && npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
python scripts/claude_e2e.py
```

Expected output: 11 `PASS` lines.

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/guarantees/

# What keelyard guarantees, and what it doesn't

keelyard is a local tool that runs as you. It makes an agent's claims checkable and its file edits undoable.
It is not a sandbox. This page lists exactly what holds and where the limits are.

## Proof

| keelyard guarantees | it does not guarantee |
|---|---|
| "proven" means a passing test run was recorded **for the current file contents**. Any change to a snapshotted file after that run (even one made without a hook firing) reopens the proof. | That your tests are good. A proof is only as strong as the test suite. |
| Evidence is shown at three levels, never merged: **test-verified** (keelyard ran the test command itself), **command-succeeded** (the agent ran tests in its shell and the agent harness reported the result), **agent-claimed** (the agent wrote it, e.g. a checklist tick or `accept-tests`). | That agent-claimed evidence is true. It is shown so you can judge it. |
| Proof bundles are signed with a key kept outside the project (`<data home>/keelyard/proof.key`, mode 600). A bundle edited by hand, or with its signature removed, is never reported as proven again in that session. | Protection against a process that deliberately reads that key. Anything running as your user can. Signing stops casual forging, not a determined attacker. |
| Weakened tests keep the proof open: deleted test files, fewer test functions or assertions, new `skip`/`xfail`/`only` markers, changed or added test config, fewer tests in the run than before. Compared against the files as they were before the session's first edit. | Catching every weakening. Changing an expected value (`== 81` to `== 90`), or a test that checks the wrong thing, still looks fine. The counts are pattern-based per language. |
| If no agent's Stop hook is wired, or a wired agent has never called keelyard, status and doctor say so in yellow and never show a green "proven". | That an agent obeys the gate. Claude Code and Codex let the Stop hook block; OpenCode cannot veto "idle", so keelyard sends the missing items as a new prompt. After `max_blocks` reminders the gate lets the agent stop and records that. |
| Parallel sessions and hooks write proof and timeline state under file locks; a torn write cannot produce a half bundle (atomic replace). | Consistency across machines or network file systems with broken locking. |

## Rewind

| keelyard guarantees | it does not guarantee |
|---|---|
| Every rewind first snapshots the current state, so it can be undone with the step number it prints. | Undoing anything outside the project folder. |
| Files a snapshot cannot hold (gitignored, secrets, larger than `max_file_mb`) but that a rewind would overwrite or delete are copied to `.keelyard/backup/<time>/` first. | Undoing **databases, migrations that ran, deployed services, sent emails, pushed commits, or package installs**. A snapshot holds files only. Before a destructive command (`rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, `DROP TABLE`, migrations) keelyard snapshots the files and warns; the database itself is not restored. |
| An interrupted rewind (crash, Ctrl-C) leaves a journal. keelyard refuses to rewind again until `keelyard rewind recover` puts back the state from just before it. | Recovery if `.keelyard/` itself is deleted. |
| Your own `.git` is never touched (separate shadow repository, own index). | |

## Secrets

- Never snapshotted by default: `.env`, `.env.*` (except `.env.example`/`.sample`/`.template`), `*.pem`, `*.key`,
  `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.jks`, `*.keystore`, `id_rsa*`/`id_ed25519*`/..., `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.netrc`,
  `.git-credentials`, `credentials.json`, `service-account*.json`, `*.tfstate`, `secrets/`. Change it with
  `[rewind].include_secrets = true` or add patterns with `[rewind].exclude`.
- Memory, proof bundles and reports pass text through a redactor (API keys, tokens, private keys, JWTs,
  `PASSWORD=...` style assignments). It is pattern-based: an unusual secret format can slip through.
- keelyard never sends anything anywhere. The only network calls are the ones you configure (swarm helper models).

## Tokens

- keelyard's own additions (brief, hints, footers) are budgeted. `keelyard run` returns the raw output when
  filtering would not save more than its own footer costs.
- Filters never drop an error or warning line: tested against real logs from pytest, cargo, go, node, eslint,
  ruff, npm and git (`tests/corpus/`), also with thousands of lines of padding.
- Six mechanisms, each with a safeguard (measured in [BENCHMARKS](BENCHMARKS.md), $0, no model):

| mechanism | what it saves | the safeguard | limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| find code (`find_symbol`, `outline`, `related`, `code find/refs/related`) | reading whole files to locate one function | ranked results never cut silently; `related` lists imports, importers and tests; `refs=true` lists call sites | regex-based, not a type checker: dynamic dispatch and re-exports can be missed |
| re-reads (`read_file`) | resending a file already in context | unchanged = short notice, changed = diff, `force=true` = full text; a notice is never sent when the file is smaller | relies on the agent still holding the earlier copy; reset on compaction |
| log compaction (`keelyard run`, `run_compact`) | passing lines and banners | errors, warnings, stack frames, test counts and the exit code are kept (corpus test); the footer says how many lines were collapsed and `keelyard recall <id>` returns the raw output | pattern-based per tool; unknown tools get the generic compressor |
| paged results (`find_symbol`, `memory_search`) | long result lists | best first, `remaining` and `next_offset` on every page; walking all pages returns everything | memory search counts at most 500 matches |
| work state (`work_state`, `keelyard state`) | re-deriving decisions after a compaction | every decision needs a ref (`path:line`, `cmd: ...`, `#proof item`), validated when added and re-checked on every render; stale refs are marked STALE | it records what the agent writes down; it does not infer decisions |
| tools per task (`[mcp].tools = "lazy"`) | tool schemas sent every request | `tool_search` finds every hidden tool, `tool_call` runs it; lazy falls back to `core` if it is not smaller | each on-demand use costs about 309 tokens; past about 4 distinct hidden tools a session is cheaper with `core`, so `core` is the default |

- Every preset adds a ~12-token terse-output rule to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md ("Be terse: no preamble or recap. Keep
  code exact."). Opt out: `keelyard init --no-terse` or `KEELYARD_TERSE=0`. On three local 0.5-1.8B models it used
  2.6% fewer total tokens than the old "Be terse" line and kept more required facts (155/192 vs 142): not a
  guarantee for other models or for every model (`BENCHMARKS.md`).
- JSON output is compacted only losslessly (minified, same-key lists as columns/rows) and only when smaller.
- A failing test run identical to an earlier failure on different code adds one ~40-token hint; nothing otherwise.
- The lean preset saves tokens partly by **turning tools off** (9 OpenCode built-ins, keelyard's MCP list).
- Benchmarks used a free model, so there is no cost claim. See [BENCHMARKS](BENCHMARKS.md) for the split
  between cached and uncached input.

## Per agent

| capability | Claude Code | Codex | OpenCode |
|---|---|---|---|
| proof gate at the end of a turn | Stop hook blocks | Stop hook blocks (approve hooks once with `/hooks`) | cannot block "idle": missing items sent as a new prompt |
| evidence from shell test runs | command-succeeded | command-succeeded | command-succeeded |
| `proof test` / `proof_run_tests` | test-verified | test-verified | test-verified (MCP off in lean: use the CLI) |
| snapshot after each edit | yes | yes | yes |
| shell output filtered in place | yes (`updatedToolOutput`) | sent the same way; not yet confirmed in a real Codex session | yes (plugin rewrites the output) |
| `[mcp].tools = "lazy"` (tool_search/tool_call) | yes | yes | only with MCP on |
| work state in the brief after compaction | yes (SessionStart `compact`) | at session start; re-sent after compaction not confirmed | yes (plugin compaction hook) |
| MCP tools | `.mcp.json` | `~/.codex/config.toml` or `--codex-project-mcp` | off by default (`KEELYARD_OPENCODE_MCP=1`) |
| checked how | scripted hook payloads in CI (`keelyard selftest`) | scripted hook payloads in CI | real sessions, OpenCode 2.0.22 on Windows 11 |

Real Claude Code and Codex sessions have not been benchmarked yet.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/guide/proof/

# Proof gate

Agents often say "done" when nothing was run, or when tests went green only because they were edited.
The proof gate is a Stop hook. If the agent changed files in this session, it cannot finish until all of
these are true:

1. There is a requirement checklist (`proof_requirements`).
2. Every item has evidence: a command and its result, or a `path:line` (`proof_check`).
3. A test run after the last edit passed (`proof_run_tests` with `phase="after"`).
4. If `[proof].app_url` is set, there is a screenshot taken since the last edit.

When something is missing, the hook answers `{"decision": "block", "reason": ...}`. The reason lists what is
missing, so the agent knows exactly what to do next. To stop loops, the gate gives up after `max_blocks`
reminders (3 by default) and tells you. A turn that changed no files and wrote no checklist is never blocked.

## The report

Each session gets a self-contained HTML file in `.keelyard/proof/<session>/report.html`. It has no external
requests and embeds its fonts, so you can attach it to a PR.

![proof report](../img/proof-report.png)

The timeline at the bottom interleaves snapshots, test runs and every gate decision.

## From the CLI

```bash
keelyard proof add "SAVE10 takes 10% off" "unknown coupons raise ValueError"
keelyard proof test before            # optional baseline
keelyard proof test after
keelyard proof check 1 "test_save10 passes"
keelyard proof status                 # exit 0 when proven, 3 when not
keelyard proof report --open
```

The test command comes from `[proof].test_cmd`. If that is not set, keelyard detects it from `package.json`,
`Cargo.toml`, `go.mod` or Python test files. To use a different command for one run, pass
`--cmd "npm test"`.

## Limits

The gate checks that evidence exists. It does not check that the evidence is true. An agent that is
determined to lie can write a false sentence. The report exists so that a person can read the evidence
in one minute.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/guide/rewind/

# Rewind

After every edit or shell command, keelyard snapshots the project into `.keelyard/shadow.git`. That is a
separate git repository: your `.git`, index, stash and branches are never touched. Snapshots follow
`.gitignore`. Files over `[rewind].max_file_mb` (20 MB by default) are skipped and listed as skipped. Nested
repositories, such as monorepo packages that have their own `.git`, are included file by file.

```bash
keelyard rewind list         # -n 100 for more, -i for the timeline browser
keelyard rewind show 12      # the diff step 12 made
keelyard rewind to 9         # files back to how they were after step 9
keelyard rewind fork 9 ../b  # copy step 9 into another folder and try a different approach there
keelyard rewind snap         # snapshot now
```

![rewind](../img/cli-rewind.png)

`rewind to` takes a snapshot of the current state first and prints its number. To undo the rewind,
rewind to that number. Files that were created after the target step are removed. Files that were
deleted are restored.

## Timeline browser

`keelyard rewind list -i` shows steps on the left and the diff of the selected step on the right. Press `r`
to rewind to the selected step.

![timeline](../img/timeline.png)

![confirm](../img/timeline-confirm.png)

## Cost

On a 7,083-file Django checkout, a snapshot after an edit takes 88 ms (median). The first snapshot takes
2.3 s, because it hashes every file. Concurrent hooks are serialised with a lock file, so two agents saving
at the same moment cannot corrupt the timeline.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/guide/context/

# Smaller context

## Output filters

`keelyard run <command>` runs a command and prints a shorter version of its output. Filters exist for
`git status/log/diff`, pytest, cargo, go and jest tests, grep and rg, find and ls, and ruff, eslint and mypy.
Every failure, error and `file:line` is kept; what is dropped is repetition and progress noise. The filtered
output is never longer than the original.

In Claude Code the same filters run on Bash results through `PostToolUse`. The command itself is not
changed, only what the model reads. Each shortened output ends with an id, and `keelyard recall <id>`
(or the MCP `recall` tool) returns the full text.

```bash
keelyard run pytest -q
keelyard run -- git log --stat -n 50
pytest -v 2>&1 | keelyard filter --for "pytest -v"
```

On 8 real commands, the filters cut 56,522 tokens to 5,901 and kept 100% of the facts we extracted
([method](../BENCHMARKS.md)).

## Deduplicated reads

When the agent reads a file it has already read in this session, and the file has not changed, keelyard
answers with a one-line notice instead of the file. If the file changed, the MCP `read_file` tool returns
only the diff. When the agent's context is compacted, this memory is cleared so it can read again.

## Structure first

- `project_map`: files per directory, with approximate token sizes
- `outline path`: classes and signatures with line numbers (Python is parsed properly; other languages use patterns)
- `find_symbol name`: where something is defined

```bash
keelyard code map
keelyard code outline src/cart.py
keelyard code find Cart
```


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/guide/memory/

# Memory and usage

## Memory

keelyard indexes the session logs that Claude Code (`~/.claude/projects`), Codex (`~/.codex/sessions`) and
OpenCode (`~/.local/share/opencode/storage`) already keep on disk. The index is SQLite FTS5, stored in
`~/.local/share/keelyard/memory.db` with mode 600. Secrets such as API keys, tokens and private keys are
redacted before anything is stored.

```bash
keelyard memory index
keelyard memory search "websocket reconnect"
keelyard memory stats
```

The agent uses the `memory_search` tool, which indexes new sessions before every search and by default
only searches sessions from the current project.

## Usage

`keelyard usage` reads the same logs and adds up input, output and cache tokens by day, model or agent.
keelyard ships no prices. To get a cost column, add `[prices."model-name"]` to the config. Models without
a price are marked rather than guessed.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/guide/brain/

# Always on

Tools only help if the agent remembers to use them. keelyard therefore puts a little of itself into the
agent's context at the moments that matter, with a hard token budget each time.

## What the agent sees, and when

| moment | what keelyard adds | budget |
|---|---|---|
| session start | a **brief**: the rules (rewind, proof, cheap exploration, helpers), open proof items, a project map digest, and past-session notes that match the current task | `brief_tokens`, 600 by default |
| after the context is compacted | the same brief again, marked "re-sent after compaction" | same |
| each prompt you send | up to 4 snippets from earlier sessions **in this project** that match the prompt. Nothing at all if none match. | `recall_tokens`, 250 by default |
| before reading a file again | if it is unchanged: "you already have it", plus its outline so the agent can find its place. If it changed: only the diff. | about 300 tokens of outline |
| before a destructive command | `rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f`, `git checkout .`, `git push --force`, `DROP`/`TRUNCATE`, `DELETE` without `WHERE`, and migrations (Django, Alembic, Prisma, Rails, Knex, Sequelize): keelyard **takes a snapshot first** and tells the agent which step restores the files. Files only: a dropped table, an applied migration or a deleted remote branch is not undone ([limits](../guarantees.md)) | one line |
| before editing code with no test nearby | "no tests found for billing.py" (looks for `test_x.py`, `x_test.go`, `x.test.ts`, `tests/` and the like) | one line, once per file |
| when the session gets large | if you set `plan_tokens`, a hint to hand bulk work to helpers once the session passes `budget_warn_at` of it | one line |

keelyard never decides for you. A destructive command is not blocked; the snapshot just makes it undoable.

## Never spammy

Every hint has a cooldown per kind (`nudge_cooldown_s`, 5 minutes) and there is a cap per session
(`max_nudges_per_session`, 12). The snapshot before a destructive command happens every time, even when the
hint itself is rate-limited.

```toml
[brain]
brief = true
brief_tokens = 600
recall = true
recall_tokens = 250
nudges = true
nudge_cooldown_s = 300
max_nudges_per_session = 12
plan_tokens = 0          # e.g. 200000; 0 turns the budget hint off
budget_warn_at = 0.6
```

Past-session recall reads keelyard's memory index. The Stop hook refreshes it at most every 10 minutes;
`keelyard memory index` does it by hand.

## Per agent

| | Claude Code | Codex | OpenCode |
|---|---|---|---|
| brief at start | SessionStart `additionalContext` | SessionStart `additionalContext` | system prompt (`experimental.chat.system.transform`) |
| brief after compaction | SessionStart with `source: compact` | **gap**: no post-compaction event | kept in the compaction summary (`experimental.session.compacting`) |
| recall per prompt | UserPromptSubmit `additionalContext` | UserPromptSubmit `additionalContext` | queued, added to the next system prompt (`chat.message`) |
| repeat read → outline/diff | PreToolUse deny with reason | **gap**: Codex has no read tool hook | tool error with the same text |
| snapshot before destructive | PreToolUse on Bash | PreToolUse on shell | `tool.execute.before` |
| hints | PreToolUse `additionalContext` + a visible `systemMessage` for destructive commands | same JSON; whether Codex shows PreToolUse context is **not verified** | queued, added to the next system prompt |
| budget hint | from `transcript_path` size | same | **gap**: no transcript path; set nothing, it stays off |

The Claude Code column is covered by the test suite at the hook level. The Codex and OpenCode columns follow
their documented hook and plugin APIs. The OpenCode plugin is one file that supports both plugin APIs
(`@opencode/plugin` 2.x `setup(ctx)` and `@opencode-ai/plugin` 1.x `server()`); a test drives both with a fake
keelyard. Results from real sessions are in [Benchmarks](../BENCHMARKS.md) once measured.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/guide/presets/

# Presets: lowest-token settings

```bash
keelyard init --preset lean          # fewest tokens
keelyard init --preset balanced      # default
keelyard init --preset max-quality   # every keelyard tool over MCP
keelyard uninstall opencode          # reverts the preset too (only what keelyard added)
```

| | lean | balanced | max-quality |
|---|---|---|---|
| Proof | tests run by keelyard after each edit, plus the agent's shell runs | from the agent's shell test runs | MCP proof tools + shell runs |
| Brief | file map, small project files (≤1,500 tokens), pre-edit test result | file map | rules + file map |
| Shell output filter | on | on | on |
| OpenCode | `agents.build` override: 1-paragraph system prompt; webfetch, websearch, subagent, skill, question, todowrite, execute (code mode), glob, grep denied; no MCP catalog | no MCP catalog | MCP server added |
| Claude Code | `.claude/settings.json` env: `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=12000`, `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000`, `DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS=1` (your values win) | hooks + MCP | hooks + MCP |
| Codex | short rules block | hooks | hooks |
| Rules block | 3 lines | 3 lines (OpenCode) / full | full |

keelyard records exactly what it added in `.keelyard/preset.json`; uninstall removes only those keys, and only if
you did not change them. If `opencode.json` already defines `agents.build`, lean leaves it alone.

Trade-offs of lean: the agent has no web access, no subagents and no glob/grep tools (it uses the shell and the
file map in keelyard's brief instead). For Codex, the cheapest effective setting is in your user config, which
keelyard does not touch: `model_reasoning_effort = "low"` for routine fixes.

Measured effect: see [BENCHMARKS](../BENCHMARKS.md#presets-measured-on-opencode-2).


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/guide/swarm/

# Swarm

Some work is wide rather than deep: answering "where is X handled" across a package, or drafting the same
small fix in five files. `swarm` sends tasks like these to a cheaper model in parallel, and never trusts
an answer it has not checked.

## Plan

`swarm_plan(goal)` (or `keelyard swarm plan "goal"`) splits a goal into one task per relevant file. It finds
the files that define the functions or classes the goal names, and gives each task a **context pack**: only
those definitions plus the file's imports, with real line numbers. No model call is involved.

```console
$ keelyard swarm plan "fix total() so SAVE10 takes 10% off" --json
{"tasks": [{"kind": "draft_edit", "files": ["cart.py"], "symbols": ["total"], ...}]}
```

## Run and check

For each task keelyard:

1. asks the helper model for a structured answer. Questions use a JSON schema (`answer`, `citations`,
   `quotes`). A fix to one definition asks for the new definition only, and keelyard builds the diff itself,
   because small models write correct code far more often than correct diffs.
2. checks it. Citations must point at real lines, and quoted code must exist. Patches must apply, then the
   tests run on a **throwaway copy** of the project. If the suite was already failing, a patch passes when it
   fixes at least one failing test and breaks none.
3. samples `best_of` answers (2 by default) and keeps a checked one. For questions it prefers the answer whose
   citations the others agree with; for patches, the smallest one that passes.
4. if none pass, retries `retries` times (1 by default) with the checker's notes, such as the failing test
   output, added to the prompt.
5. if it still fails, tries once with `escalate_model` (`[models.strong]`) when that is configured.

Nothing is applied to your files. The agent gets the checked patch and decides.

## Your agent's own subagents

With no helper model configured, `swarm` returns `subagent_tasks`: one ready prompt per task, with the context
pack and the required output format. Hand them to the Claude Code Task tool or OpenCode subagents, then check
what comes back with `swarm_verify`. `keelyard swarm plan "goal" --subagents` prints the same prompts.

## Cooperative mode (default)

`swarm` runs as a team, not as separate calls:

- **Planner → workers → verifier.** `swarm_plan` (or `keelyard swarm plan`) splits the goal. Workers draft,
  and keelyard checks every draft (citations exist, the patch applies and passes the tests in a copy).
- **Blackboard.** What one worker got verified, and what was tried and rejected, goes into the prompt of the
  next worker on the same files, capped at 1,200 characters.
- **Critic.** Each candidate that passes the checks is reviewed by a second call (`APPROVE` or
  `REJECT: reason`). A rejection sends the task back with the reason. Off by default (`critic = true` turns it on): with a
  1.5B model it doubled the tokens and caught nothing the tests didn't (see below).
- **Voting.** Among accepted candidates, the one most others agree with wins (same changed lines, or the
  same cited lines).
- **Cheapest capable model.** Tasks start on the first model in `ladder` and move up only when the checks
  fail. When a model keeps failing a kind of task (fewer than 1 in 3 after 3 tries), later tasks of that
  kind start one step higher.
- **Hard token budget.** Every call reserves its worst case (prompt characters / 3 plus `max_tokens`) before
  it is sent. A call that would cross `budget_tokens` or `task_budget_tokens` is refused, and the task
  reports `stopped: ... budget ... reached`. Results include `tokens`, `tokens_by_model` and
  `tokens_per_verified`.
- **Many workers.** `workers` sets how many tasks run at once. The tests run 250 tasks with more than 200
  calls in flight, and the token total matches exactly.

`keelyard swarm run tasks.json --basic`, or `cooperative = false`, gives the plain swarm.

## Configure

```toml
[models.cheap]
provider = "openai"            # any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, e.g. Ollama or vLLM
base_url = "http://localhost:11434/v1"
model = "qwen2.5-coder:7b"

[swarm]
best_of = 2
retries = 1
escalate_model = "strong"      # "" turns escalation off
test_patches = true
cooperative = true
ladder = ["cheap", "strong"]   # cheapest first; [] = helper_model then escalate_model
workers = 64
critic = false
budget_tokens = 200000         # hard cap per swarm call, 0 = none
task_budget_tokens = 20000
```

## Measured

On 5 small bug fixes with a 1.5B local model, the old single-shot swarm got 0 right and marked 2-3 wrong
patches as verified. The new pipeline got 4 of 5 right in both runs and marked no wrong patch verified, using
about half the input tokens. For questions, "verified" only means the cited lines exist: 5 were verified, 2-3
were right. Details: [Benchmarks](../BENCHMARKS.md#swarm-quality).

Cooperative mode, 2 runs × 10 tasks: pipeline 15/20 at 1,272 tokens per correct, best-local 18/20 at 1,560 tokens per correct, coop-nocritic 15/20 at 1,312 tokens per correct, coop 15/20 at 2,943 tokens per correct.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/guide/arena/

# Arena

The arena runs the same task across several agents and models. Each run gets a fresh copy of the
repository, and the task's check command decides pass or fail. Tokens and cost come from each agent's own
machine-readable output. If an agent reports nothing, the cell says `n/a`. Nothing is estimated.

```bash
keelyard arena run examples/arena/discount/task.toml --out arena-results
keelyard arena render arena-results       # re-render from results.json
```

`task.local.toml` runs without any agent CLI or API key. It uses a local model through Ollama and two
baselines: "do nothing" and the reference fix.

![arena report](../img/arena-report.png)

The report above is a real run: the 1.5B one-shot contender passed 0 of 5. We have not run
Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode through the arena on this machine yet. When we do, the results go in
[Benchmarks](../BENCHMARKS.md).

Agent CLI flags change between releases. Check the `cmd` lines in `task.toml` against the versions you
have installed.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/guide/agents/

# For agents

keelyard is meant to be driven by agents. Everything a person can do from the CLI, an agent can do through
MCP, and both return JSON.

## What `init` installs

| agent | hooks | MCP | instructions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `.claude/settings.json` | `.mcp.json` | `CLAUDE.md` section, `.claude/skills/keelyard/SKILL.md`, `/keelyard:status`, `/keelyard:prove`, `/keelyard:undo` |
| Codex | `.codex/hooks.json` | snippet for `~/.codex/config.toml`, or `.codex/config.toml` with `--codex-project-mcp` | `AGENTS.md` section |
| OpenCode | `.opencode/plugins/keelyard.js` | `opencode.json` | `AGENTS.md` section |

The instruction sections sit between `<!-- keelyard:start -->` and `<!-- keelyard:end -->`. `init` replaces only
that block, and `uninstall` removes only that block. The rest of the file stays as you wrote it.

## The loop an agent follows

1. `proof_requirements(items=[...])`
2. `project_map`, `find_symbol`, `outline`, then `read_file`
3. edit (snapshots happen automatically)
4. `run_compact` for tests and builds
5. `proof_run_tests(phase="after")`, then `proof_check` for each item
6. `proof_status` → `{"proven": true}`

All 20 tools are listed, with their schemas, in the [MCP reference](../mcp.md).

## Self-test

`keelyard selftest` plays the agent. It sends the same hook JSON Claude Code sends and does everything else
through the MCP server over stdio. In a temporary project it records requirements, reads code, searches
memory, runs a swarm task against a local stub model, makes a bad edit, gets blocked by the gate, rewinds,
fixes the bug, proves it and is let through. It needs no network and no API key.

![selftest](../img/cli-selftest.png)

### Codex: checked version

Checked against **Codex CLI 0.165.0** (Oct 28, 2026) with `scripts/codex_e2e.py`, which runs the real Codex binary
against a local scripted model (no API key) and runs in CI on every push and weekly. All five hooks fire, the proof
gate blocks a "done" with red tests and opens after a passing shell test run, MCP tools and the AGENTS.md block reach
the model, and rewind restores an edit. Codex sends shell results to `PostToolUse` as a plain string with no exit
code; keelyard reads the test result from the output. See [Codex in 2 minutes](../codex.md).

### Codex MCP: project or user level

Codex reads MCP servers from `~/.codex/config.toml`, and from a project's `.codex/config.toml` only when you
trust the project. keelyard never writes either without asking:

- `keelyard init --codex-project-mcp` (or `keelyard install codex --codex-project-mcp`) adds the server to this
  project's `.codex/config.toml`, between `# keelyard:start` / `# keelyard:end`. Trust the project in Codex once.
- `keelyard install codex --global` adds it to `~/.codex/config.toml` for every project.

`keelyard doctor` warns if Codex hooks are wired but neither file has the server. `keelyard uninstall codex`
removes the block and deletes the file if nothing else was in it.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/cli/

# CLI reference

Generated from `keelyard --help` by `docs/demo/gen_reference.py`.

Every command accepts `--json` and prints exactly one JSON object with `ok` and `exit` keys.

```text
usage: keelyard <command> [options]

keelyard makes coding agents prove their work, lets you undo any step,
and keeps their context small. Works with Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode.

start here:
  init              set up this project and wire every agent it finds
  doctor            check that everything is installed and wired correctly
  status            what keelyard knows about this project right now

everyday:
  rewind            list, inspect and undo agent steps
  proof             the evidence an agent collected before saying "done"
  run               run a command and print a compact version of its output
  code              outline a file, map the project, find a symbol
  memory            search past sessions across all your agents
  usage             tokens and cost from your local agent logs

more:
  swarm             fan small, checkable tasks out to a cheap model
  arena             run one task across agents and models, compare results
  bench             measure savings on your own machine
  selftest          a scripted agent completes a full task through the agent interface
  install/uninstall wire or unwire one agent by hand
  filter            compact output piped on stdin
  recall            print the full output that `run` shortened

options:
  -h, --help   show this help message and exit
  --version    show program's version number and exit

commands:
  <command>
    init       set up this project and wire the agents found on this machine
    doctor     check the installation and wiring; exits 3 if something is broken
    status     show what keelyard knows about this project
    selftest   a scripted agent runs a full task through MCP and hooks in a temp folder
    install    wire one agent in this project
    uninstall  unwire one agent in this project
    rewind     list, inspect and undo agent steps
    proof      the evidence an agent collected before saying done
    run        run a command and print a compact version of its output
    filter     compact output piped on stdin
    recall     print the full output that `run` shortened
    code       outline a file, map the project, find a symbol
    memory     search past sessions across all your agents
    state      compact work state: requirements, decisions, changes, open questions
    usage      tokens and cost from your local agent logs
    swarm      fan small, checkable tasks out to a cheap model
    arena      run one task across agents and models, compare results
    bench      measure savings on your own machine

exit codes:
  0  success
  1  error (the message says what went wrong and how to fix it)
  2  usage error (bad command or arguments)
  3  a check did not pass (doctor found a problem, proof not complete, tests failed, selftest failed)
  `keelyard run` exits with the code of the command it ran.

Run `keelyard <command> --help` for examples. Every command accepts --json.
```

## init

```text
usage: keelyard init [-h] [--json] [--agent {claude,codex,opencode}] [--no-agents] [--dry-run]
                     [--preset {lean,balanced,max-quality}] [--codex-project-mcp] [--no-terse]
                     [--global]

set up this project and wire the agents found on this machine

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json                print one JSON object on stdout (for scripts and agents)
  --agent {claude,codex,opencode}
                        wire only this agent (repeatable)
  --no-agents           create the config but wire no agent
  --dry-run             print what would change and stop
  --preset {lean,balanced,max-quality}
                        lean = fewest tokens (trimmed agent prompt/tools, capped output); balanced
                        = default; max-quality = every keelyard tool over MCP. `keelyard uninstall
                        <agent>` reverts it
  --codex-project-mcp   Codex: register the keelyard MCP server in this project's
                        .codex/config.toml instead of asking you to edit ~/.codex/config.toml
                        (Codex reads it only for trusted projects)
  --no-terse            leave out the terse-output rule (results only, no filler) from
                        CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md
  --global              wire the agents for every project of this user (~/.claude, ~/.codex,
                        ~/.config/opencode); projects set themselves up on their first session

examples:
  keelyard init                    # detect agents, wire them, take a first snapshot
  keelyard init --agent claude     # only Claude Code
  keelyard init --dry-run          # show what would change
```

## rewind

```text
usage: keelyard rewind [-h] [--json] <action> ...

list, inspect and undo agent steps

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print one JSON object on stdout (for scripts and agents)

actions:
  <action>
    list      list snapshots
    show      show the diff a step made
    to        restore files to a step (undoable)
    fork      copy a step into a new folder
    snap      take a snapshot now
    recover   finish a rewind that was interrupted (puts back the state from just before it)

examples:
  keelyard rewind                  # every step agents took, newest last
  keelyard rewind list -i          # browse steps and diffs full-screen
  keelyard rewind show 12          # the diff that step 12 made
  keelyard rewind to 9             # put the files back as they were after step 9
  keelyard rewind fork 9 ../try-b  # copy step 9 into another folder
  keelyard rewind snap             # take a snapshot by hand
```

```text
usage: keelyard code [-h] [--json] <action> ...

outline a file, map the project, find a symbol

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print one JSON object on stdout (for scripts and agents)

actions:
  <action>
    outline   signatures only
    map       compact project map
    find      where a symbol is defined (best first, paged)
    related   what a file imports, who imports it, and its tests

examples:
  keelyard code outline src/app.py
  keelyard code map
  keelyard code find Cart
```

## swarm

```text
usage: keelyard swarm [-h] [--json] <action> ...

fan small, checkable tasks out to a cheap model

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print one JSON object on stdout (for scripts and agents)

  <action>
    run       run tasks from a JSON file
    plan      split a goal into focused helper tasks (no model call)

examples:
  keelyard swarm plan "fix total() for SAVE10" --json > tasks.json
  keelyard swarm run tasks.json   # [{"kind": "ask", "prompt": "...", "files": ["a.py"], "symbols": ["total"]}]

```

```text
  tasks

  --best-of BEST_OF  samples per task (default: [swarm].best_of)
  --retries RETRIES  retries with checker feedback (default: [swarm].retries)
  --basic            no blackboard, critic, routing or budget (the plain swarm)
```
