URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/mcp/

# MCP reference

Generated from the running server by `docs/demo/gen_reference.py`.

The server is `keelyard mcp` (stdio). It sends these instructions to the agent on connect:

```text
keelyard: proof, rewind, smaller context. For a change: proof_requirements -> find_symbol,
read_file(ranges) -> edit (auto-snapshotted; rewind_to undoes) -> run_compact -> proof_run_tests(phase="after")
-> proof_check each item -> proof_status proven. Step-by-step guides: workflow("plan"|"debug"|"review").
```

Every tool returns a JSON object (MCP structured content). Errors are MCP tool errors whose text says what went wrong and, where there is one, a `Hint:` with the fix.

These are the default (`core`) tools. `[mcp].tools = "all"` adds the rest; `"lazy"` sends only `read_file`, `run_compact`, `find_symbol` and `proof_status` plus `tool_search` (find a hidden tool and its schema) and `tool_call` (run it), and falls back to `core` if that would not be smaller.

| tool | read-only | destructive | summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`proof_requirements`](#proof_requirements) |  |  | Record what the user asked for as a checklist. Call this first. Duplicate items are ignored. |
| [`proof_check`](#proof_check) |  |  | Mark one requirement as verified, with concrete evidence (a command and its result, or file:line). |
| [`proof_run_tests`](#proof_run_tests) |  |  | Run the project's tests and record the result as evidence. |
| [`proof_status`](#proof_status) | yes |  | Is the work proven? Returns {"proven", "missing": [what to do next], "requirements", "report"}. |
| [`rewind_list`](#rewind_list) | yes |  | List recent workspace snapshots, oldest first. One is taken after every edit or shell command. |
| [`rewind_to`](#rewind_to) |  | yes | Restore project files to how they were after `step`. A safety snapshot is taken first, |
| [`read_file`](#read_file) | yes |  | Read a project file. A repeat read of an unchanged file returns a one-line notice instead of the |
| [`run_compact`](#run_compact) |  |  | Run a command and return output with failures, errors and file:line kept and noise dropped. |
| [`recall`](#recall) | yes |  | Return the full raw output that run_compact or the shell-output filter shortened. |
| [`find_symbol`](#find_symbol) | yes |  | Where is a symbol defined (best match first), and with refs=true where it is used. |
| [`swarm`](#swarm) |  |  | Run small tasks on the configured helper model in parallel. Each answer is checked: citations (path:line) |
| [`memory_search`](#memory_search) | yes |  | Search past Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions, best match first. New sessions are indexed first. |
| [`work_state`](#work_state) |  |  | Compact state that survives compaction: requirements, decisions, changed files, open questions. |
| [`workflow`](#workflow) | yes |  | A short step-by-step guide: plan (plan-implement-verify), debug (loop), review (diff checklist). |

## proof_requirements

Record what the user asked for as a checklist. Call this first. Duplicate items are ignored.

Returns {"requirements": [{"id", "text", "done", "evidence"}]}.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | array | required | One short, checkable item per user ask, e.g. ["discount applies once", "empty cart costs 0"]. |

## proof_check

Mark one requirement as verified, with concrete evidence (a command and its result, or file:line).

Returns the updated requirement.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requirement_id` | integer | required | The id from proof_requirements, e.g. 1. |
| `evidence` | string | required | What you ran or saw, e.g. "pytest tests/test_cart.py::test_once passed" or "cart.py:14 caps at one use". |

## proof_run_tests

Run the project's tests and record the result as evidence.

Returns {"exit", "passed", "seconds", "cmd", "output"} where output is a compact tail.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `phase` | "before" / "after" | "after" | "before" your change (baseline) or "after" it (required by the gate). |
| `command` | string | "" | Optional override, e.g. "pytest -q tests/test_cart.py". Default: [proof].test_cmd or auto-detected. |

## proof_status

Is the work proven? Returns {"proven", "missing": [what to do next], "requirements", "report"}.

No parameters.

## rewind_list

List recent workspace snapshots, oldest first. One is taken after every edit or shell command.

Returns {"steps": [{"step", "tool", "ts", "files", "n_files"}], "total"}.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `last` | integer | 20 | How many recent steps, e.g. 20. |

## rewind_to

Restore project files to how they were after `step`. A safety snapshot is taken first,
so calling rewind_to(safety_step) undoes this. Returns {"restored", "removed", "safety_step", "new_step"}.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step` | integer | required | A step number from rewind_list, e.g. 3. |

## read_file

Read a project file. A repeat read of an unchanged file returns a one-line notice instead of the
text; a changed file returns only the diff since your last read. Returns {"path", "content"}.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | required | Project-relative path, e.g. "src/cart.py". Windows separators are accepted. |
| `start` | integer | 1 | First line, 1-based. |
| `end` | integer | 0 | Last line, inclusive; 0 = end of file. |
| `force` | boolean | false | Return the full text even if you read it before (e.g. after compaction). |

## run_compact

Run a command and return output with failures, errors and file:line kept and noise dropped.
Returns {"exit", "output"}; the output ends with an id for recall() when anything was cut.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string | required | Command line, run without a shell, e.g. "pytest -q" or "git log -n 20". |
| `timeout` | integer | 600 | Seconds before the command is killed. |

## recall

Return the full raw output that run_compact or the shell-output filter shortened.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `output_id` | string | required | The id printed by run_compact, e.g. "3f9a1c2b7d4e". |

## find_symbol

Where is a symbol defined (best match first), and with refs=true where it is used.
Returns {"matches": [...], "remaining", "next_offset"?}; results are paged, never cut silently.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | Function, class or type name, e.g. "Cart". |
| `refs` | boolean | false | Also list call sites and uses (source before tests). |
| `offset` | integer | 0 | Skip this many results; use next_offset from the last call. |

## swarm

Run small tasks on the configured helper model in parallel. Each answer is checked: citations (path:line)
must exist; drafts must apply and pass the tests in a throwaway copy (never applied to your files).
Failed answers are retried with the checker's notes, best-of-N, then escalated to the strong model if set.
With no helper model configured, returns {"mode": "plan", "subagent_tasks": [...]} for your own subagents.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tasks` | array | required | Each: {"kind": "ask"|"summarize"|"draft_edit"|"grep", "prompt": str, "files": [paths], "symbols": [names]}. "symbols" narrows the context to those definitions. Tip: swarm_plan builds this list for you. Example: [{"kind": "ask", "prompt": "Where is the discount applied?", "files": ["cart.py"]}] |

## memory_search

Search past Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions, best match first. New sessions are indexed first.
Returns {"hits": [{"agent", "session", "project", "ts", "role", "snippet"}], "remaining", "next_offset"?}.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | required | Words to look for, e.g. "stripe webhook signature". |
| `this_project_only` | boolean | true | Only sessions that ran in this project. |
| `budget_chars` | integer | 2400 | Max characters of snippets returned. |
| `offset` | integer | 0 | Skip this many hits; use next_offset from the last call. |

## work_state

Compact state that survives compaction: requirements, decisions, changed files, open questions.
Record each key decision with a ref to the file line or command that backs it.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | "show" / "decision" / "question" / "resolve" | "show" | show, record, or resolve. |
| `text` | string | "" | The decision or question, one line. |
| `ref` | string | "" | Evidence: "path:line", "cmd: <command>" or "#<proof item>". Required for decisions. |
| `item` | integer | 0 | Id to resolve. |

## workflow

A short step-by-step guide: plan (plan-implement-verify), debug (loop), review (diff checklist).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | "plan" / "debug" / "review" | required | Which guide. |


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/config/

# Configuration

`keelyard init` writes `.keelyard/config.toml`. Every field is optional. This is the default file:

```toml
# keelyard configuration. Every field is optional.

[proof]
# Block the agent from finishing until a proof bundle exists.
gate = true
# Command used for before/after test runs. Empty = auto-detect.
test_cmd = ""
# URL of the running app; when set, a screenshot is required for proof.
app_url = ""
# Stop the gate from looping forever: give up after this many blocks per session.
max_blocks = 3

[rewind]
enabled = true
# Files larger than this are left out of snapshots and listed as skipped.
max_file_mb = 20
# Tools that trigger a snapshot after they run.
snapshot_tools = ["Write", "Edit", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit", "Bash", "apply_patch", "write", "edit", "bash", "patch"]

[swarm]
# Max concurrent helper calls.
concurrency = 16
# Hard cap on tasks per swarm call.
max_tasks = 256
# Which [models.*] entry helpers use.
helper_model = "cheap"
# Samples per task (best-of-N), retries with verifier feedback, and the model tried once when all fail
# ("" = no escalation). Draft patches are also run against the tests in a temporary copy.
best_of = 2
retries = 1
escalate_model = "strong"
test_patches = true
# Cooperative mode (default; `keelyard swarm run --basic` turns it off for one run): models tried cheapest first
# ([] = helper_model then escalate_model), concurrent workers, a peer critic, and hard token caps
# (0 = no cap). Calls are refused before they are made once a cap would be crossed.
cooperative = true
ladder = []
workers = 64
critic = false
budget_tokens = 200000
task_budget_tokens = 20000

[mcp]
# Tools the MCP server offers. Every schema costs tokens in every session, so the default is the 14 the
# workflow needs. "all" adds outline, project_map, rewind_diff, usage_report, route_task, swarm_plan,
# swarm_verify, status (and proof_screenshot, which "core" adds by itself when [proof].app_url is set).
# "lazy" sends only read_file, run_compact, find_symbol, proof_status plus tool_search/tool_call (about 60%
# fewer schema tokens than "core"); every other tool is found and run on demand. It falls back to "core"
# by itself if it would not be smaller.
tools = "core"

[saver]
# Deny a repeat Read of an unchanged file (reset on context compaction).
dedupe_reads = true
# Filter large Bash results before the model reads them (raw output kept for `keelyard recall`).
filter_bash = true
filter_min_chars = 1200
# Max characters returned by compress_output before head/tail trimming.
max_output_chars = 6000

# Optional prices for `keelyard usage`, USD per million tokens. keelyard ships none.
# [prices."your-model-name"]
# input = 0.0
# output = 0.0
# cache_read = 0.0
# cache_write = 0.0

# Models are plain names you choose; keelyard never assumes a vendor's lineup.
# provider = "openai" (any OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions) or "anthropic".
[models.cheap]
provider = "openai"
base_url = "http://localhost:11434/v1"
model = "qwen2.5-coder:7b"
api_key_env = ""

[models.strong]
provider = "anthropic"
base_url = "https://api.anthropic.com"
model = "set-me"
api_key_env = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

`.keelyard/` also holds snapshots (`shadow.git`, `steps.jsonl`), proof bundles, shortened outputs (`raw/`)
and the hook error log (`hook.log`). The folder contains a `.gitignore` with `*`, so it is never committed.

Environment variables:

| variable | effect |
|---|---|
| `KEELYARD_ROOT` | use this folder as the project root instead of searching upward for `.keelyard` or `.git` |
| `XDG_DATA_HOME` | where the memory index lives (default `~/.local/share/keelyard`) |
| `NO_COLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR=0` | plain terminal output |


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/json/

# Exit codes and JSON

| code | meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | success |
| `1` | error. The message says what went wrong, and a `hint:` line says what to do. |
| `2` | usage error: unknown command, missing or bad argument |
| `3` | a check did not pass: `doctor` found a problem, `proof status` is not proven, `proof test` failed, `selftest` failed |

`keelyard run` exits with the exit code of the command it ran.

With `--json`, a command prints exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else. The object always has
`ok` and `exit`:

```json
{"proven": false, "missing": ["Requirement #2 not verified: unknown coupons raise ValueError"], "ok": false, "exit": 3}
```

Errors keep the same shape:

```json
{"ok": false, "exit": 1, "error": "no step 42 (steps 1-4 exist).", "hint": "run `keelyard rewind list`."}
```

![json](img/cli-json.png)


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/troubleshooting/

# Troubleshooting

Start with `keelyard doctor`. Every failing line includes a hint.

**The agent is not blocked or snapshotted.** Run `keelyard doctor` and check the agents section. For Codex,
run `/hooks` in Codex and trust the keelyard hooks. Hooks call `keelyard` by its full path, so if you reinstall
keelyard somewhere else, run `keelyard init` again.

**Something failed silently.** Hooks never break your agent: they log the error and let the agent continue.
The log is `.keelyard/hook.log`, and `doctor` shows the last entry.

**"not a git repository or keelyard project".** keelyard refuses to snapshot your home folder or `/`. Run
`keelyard init` in the project folder.

**A large file is missing from a snapshot.** It is over `[rewind].max_file_mb`. `keelyard rewind list --json`
lists skipped files for each step.

**"no test command found".** Set `[proof].test_cmd`, or pass `--cmd`.

**The gate keeps blocking.** After `max_blocks` reminders (3 by default) it gives up and says so. To turn the
gate off, set `[proof].gate = false`.

**The project is in a path with spaces or non-ASCII characters.** Both are supported and covered by tests. If
something breaks, please open an issue and include the output of `keelyard doctor --json`.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/faq/

# FAQ

Short answers to the questions people ask about keelyard. Every claim links to the page with the details.

## What is keelyard?

keelyard is an open-source (Apache-2.0) command-line tool and MCP server that makes AI coding agents
(Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode) prove their work with a passing test run before they can finish, snapshots
every edit so any step can be undone, and trims noisy tool output. It runs locally, with no telemetry.

## How do I make Claude Code or Codex prove the tests pass before it says "done"?

Install keelyard and wire it into the project:

```bash
pipx install keelyard
keelyard init --agent claude     # or: --agent codex
```

This adds a `Stop` hook. When the agent changed files and tries to finish without a passing test run after its
last edit, the hook blocks it and says what is missing. A test run in the agent's own shell counts as proof.
See [Proof gate](guide/proof.md), [Claude Code in 2 minutes](claude-code.md) and [Codex in 2 minutes](codex.md).

## Can the agent cheat by deleting or weakening tests?

keelyard keeps the proof open when tests are deleted, when there are fewer test functions or assertions, when new
`skip`/`xfail`/`only` markers appear, or when fewer tests run than before. It does **not** catch every weakening:
changing an expected value still looks fine. Details: [Guarantees and limits](guarantees.md).

## How do I roll back a bad step an AI coding agent made?

keelyard snapshots the project after every edit and shell command, in a separate git directory
(`.keelyard/shadow.git`), so your own `.git` is never touched.

```bash
keelyard rewind list
keelyard rewind to 3
```

A rewind first snapshots the current state, so it can be undone too. Snapshots hold files only: databases,
pushed commits and package installs are not restored. See [Rewind](guide/rewind.md).

## How do I reduce the tokens a coding agent uses?

keelyard's `lean` preset (the default for `init`) caps tool output, filters noisy logs (test runners, git, package
managers) and gives the agent smaller code views. On our own benchmark of six tasks run in OpenCode
(3–8 runs per setup), whole-session tokens went from 267,525 to 52,745 (−80%) with equal or better correctness.
That is one benchmark on one agent with small samples; savings on Claude Code and Codex are not measured yet.
See [Benchmarks](BENCHMARKS.md) and [Presets](guide/presets.md).

## Does it need an API key or send my code anywhere?

No. keelyard runs on your machine and makes no network calls, except to model endpoints you configure yourself
for the optional `swarm` and `coop` commands. The end-to-end checks in CI use a local scripted model, so they
need no key either.

## Which agents and platforms are supported?

Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode, on Linux, macOS and Windows, with Python 3.11+. Claude Code and Codex are
checked end to end in CI on every push with the real CLIs. See [For agents](guide/agents.md).

## How is keelyard different from other tools?

Most related tools do one thing: shrink output, pack the repo, or track usage. keelyard's main job is the proof
gate plus undo, with output trimming as a side benefit. See [Alternatives](alternatives.md).

## How do I remove it?

`keelyard uninstall claude` (or `codex`, `opencode`) restores the files `init` changed. `keelyard uninstall
--global` does the same for user-level config.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/alternatives/

# keelyard alternatives and comparisons

What other tools do, and when you might want them instead of, or next to, keelyard. Facts about other projects
come from their own READMEs; numbers are only ours where we say "measured". Full table: [Landscape](landscape.md).

## Built-in agent features

| need | built into the agent | what keelyard adds |
|---|---|---|
| Undo an edit | Claude Code has `/rewind` checkpoints and OpenCode has `/undo`, each for edits made in its own sessions | snapshots after **every** edit and shell command, across all three agents, in a separate git dir; rewind is itself undoable |
| Run tests | every agent can run tests when it decides to | a `Stop` hook that **blocks** finishing until a passing run after the last edit is recorded, and keeps the proof open if tests were weakened |
| Project rules | `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` | a short block in those files plus hooks, so the rule is enforced, not only stated |

## Output and context tools

- **rtk**: per-command output filters. On our 8 test commands we measured 56,522 → 5,747 tokens for rtk and
  5,901 for keelyard. Use rtk if you only want output filtering.
- **repomix**, **code2prompt**: pack a repository into one prompt. Good for one-shot chats; keelyard instead gives
  the agent ranked slices (`find_symbol`, outlines) during a session.
- **serena**: symbol-level navigation and editing over LSP. Deeper code intelligence than keelyard's `find_symbol`.
- **ccusage**: usage reports from local logs. keelyard's `usage` does a similar job across Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode.

## Workflow packs

- **superpowers**, **spec-kit**: skills and spec-to-task workflows. keelyard ships small plan / review / debug
  commands, but its focus is enforcing proof, not planning.

## When keelyard is not the right tool

- You need a sandbox. keelyard runs as your user and is not a security boundary ([Guarantees](guarantees.md)).
- Your project has no tests. The proof gate can only check what your test suite checks.
- You need to undo database changes, deployments or pushed commits. Snapshots hold files only.


---

URL: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/BENCHMARKS/

# Benchmarks

!!! tip "Rerun them yourself"
    `make bench` (offline, $0) and `make codex-e2e` reproduce these numbers and the Codex check. Commands and
    methodology: [BENCHMARKS.md in the repo](https://github.com/akobirjontulqinovfuture/keelyard/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md#rerun-everything-in-one-command).

Machine: 8 vCPU Linux box, no GPU, Python 3.13. Measured on 2026-10-12. Token counts are `chars / 4`.

## Terse-output rule, measured on local models (Oct 17, 2026)

`python bench/terse.py --models qwen2.5-0.5b,llama3.2-1b,qwen-coder-1.5b --seeds 1,2` (Ollama, Q4, temperature 0.3):
32 coding prompts x 2 seeds = 64 answers per model and rule. Tokens are Ollama's own counts, input
(`prompt_eval_count`, so the rule's cost is included) + output (`eval_count`). "Facts" = the answer contains
what the prompt needs (identifier, fix, error name). Raw numbers: `bench/terse.json`. $0, no paid calls.

| rule | total tokens (3 models) | facts (of 192) |
|---|---:|---:|
| old "Be terse: no preamble, no restating the question, no summary of what you are about to do." | 24,053 | 142 |
| previous rule ("Reply with results only: ... exact and complete.", ~33 tokens) | 31,870 | 150 |
| **shipped: "Be terse: no preamble or recap. Keep code exact."** (~12 tokens) | **23,428 (−2.6% vs old)** | **155** |
| "Be terse. Keep code and facts." | 27,310 | 158 |
| "Be terse: answer first, no preamble or recap; keep code and facts complete." | 28,827 | 155 |

Per model (total / facts): qwen2.5-0.5b old 9,444/44, shipped 8,271/45; llama3.2-1b old 6,884/45,
previous 10,799/52, shipped 7,022/49; qwen-coder-1.5b old 7,725/53, previous 12,342/51, shipped 8,135/61.

- The shipped rule beats the old line on total tokens and the previous rule on facts summed over three models,
  but not on every model: on llama3.2-1b it uses 2% more tokens than the old line and keeps fewer facts than the
  previous rule. The token margin over the old line is small. Not measured with Claude or GPT models.
- Lossless JSON compaction: pretty `gh search repos --json` output 2,121 → 1,236 tokens (−42%), decoded back
  exactly (`bench/mechanisms.py`). An already-minified GitHub issue list shrank only 3%.
- The repeated-failure hint (about 40 tokens, only when it fires) was not measured for savings.

## Token-saving mechanisms, measured locally (Oct 16, 2026)

`python bench/mechanisms.py` (no model, no network, $0). Tokens are `chars / 4`. Fixtures: this repo,
the installed `httpx` package source, and the two-file `examples/arena/discount/repo`. The keelyard row shifts a little with every commit (it measures itself). Each row compares
keelyard with what an agent does without it, and checks the agent still gets what it needs.
Raw numbers: [`bench/mechanisms.json`](https://github.com/akobirjontulqinovfuture/keelyard/blob/main/bench/mechanisms.json).

| mechanism | baseline | keelyard | keelyard repo | httpx | discount (2 files) | correctness check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 find code | grep the name, read the whole defining file | ranked `find_symbol` page + outline + the definition's lines + `related` | 16,969 → 3,691 (−78%) | 54,731 → 16,717 (−69%) | 107 → 108 (**+1%**) | the definition is in the slice read |
| 2 re-reads | read, re-read, read after a 1-line edit (5 largest files) | full, "unchanged" notice, diff | 127,392 → 43,289 (−66%) | 146,937 → 49,689 (−66%) | 456 → 387 (−15%) | diff applied to the first read = the edited file; `force=true` returns all of it |
| 3 logs, real `pytest -v` | raw output | `filter_output` | 1,233 → 9 (all passed) | – | 401 → 149 (−63%, 2 failures) | every error/failure/count line kept; failing test ids kept |
| 3 logs, corpus (10 tools, pytest padded with 300 passes) | raw | filtered | 7,965 → 1,502 (−81%) | | | same |
| 4 paging | every match in one response | first page of 20 + `remaining`/`next_offset` | 8,849 → 416 (−95%) | 7,007 → 324 (−95%) | 99 → 99 (0%) | walking every page returns every result in order |
| 5 work state | re-read the 3 changed files after a compaction (modeled) | `work_state` render | 26,574 → 241 | 33,055 → 182 | 177 → 111 | every ref resolves to a real file line or command |
| 6 tool schemas per request | `core` (14 tools) | `lazy` (6 tools) | 2,319 → 927 (−60%) | | | every hidden core tool is found by `tool_search` |

What this does not show:
- Row 1 on a tiny repo is **one token worse**: when the file is smaller than an outline, just read it.
- Row 4 saves only when the answer is on the first page; reading every page costs slightly more than one dump.
- Row 5's baseline is a model of what an agent re-reads, not a measured session.
- Row 6: each on-demand tool use (search + call) adds about 309 tokens that stay in context, so `lazy` is
  smaller only while a session uses fewer than 4 distinct hidden tools. The proof workflow alone uses about 4,
  which is why `core` stays the default and `lazy` is opt-in.
- None of this was measured in a live agent session.

## Head-to-head with rtk (`bench/vs_rtk.py`)

```bash
gh release download -R rtk-ai/rtk -p 'rtk-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz' && tar xzf rtk-*.tar.gz
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/django/django /tmp/djb
git clone --depth 80 https://github.com/psf/requests /tmp/req
python bench/vs_rtk.py --rtk ./rtk --django /tmp/djb --history /tmp/req --json bench/vs_rtk_results.json
python bench/plot_vs_rtk.py
```

The script builds scratch repos: a Django clone with 5 edited files, 3 untracked and 1 deleted; a pytest project with
4 failing tests out of 125; and a Rust crate with 2 failing tests out of 42. It runs each command once and feeds the
same raw output to keelyard, while rtk runs the command itself. `FORCE_COLOR` is removed and `NO_COLOR=1` is set
for all runs. "Facts" are extracted from the raw output with fixed rules (see `facts_*` in the script) and count as
kept when every part appears verbatim in the filtered text.

| command | facts | raw tok | keelyard tok | keelyard kept | rtk tok | rtk kept |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| git status | 9 | 161 | 61 | 100% | 58 | 100% |
| git log -n 40 (requests) | 40 | 6,807 | 950 | 100% | 2,378 | 100% |
| git diff | 91 | 1,653 | 1,064 | 100% | 1,557 | 100% |
| grep -rn (django) | 15 | 277 | 230 | 100% | 277 | 100% |
| find *.py (admin) | 30 | 299 | 136 | 100% | 113 | 100% |
| ruff check (django/utils) | 307 | 43,582 | 3,022 | 100% | 1,050 | 24% |
| pytest -v (4 failing of 125) | 7 | 3,289 | 312 | 100% | 195 | 71% |
| cargo test (2 failing of 42) | 6 | 454 | 126 | 100% | 119 | 100% |
| **total** | | 56,522 | 5,901 | | 5,747 | |

Caveats: one run per command, eight commands, fact rules written by us. rtk drops line numbers from ruff results and
some assertion lines from pytest, which is why its retention is lower on those two. rtk handles many more tools.

## Output compression (`keelyard bench`, section `compress`)

The corpus is in `bench/corpus/`. Each file is real output from a real command run on the box, with temporary paths
rewritten to `/tmp/demo`:

| Log | Command | Raw | Compressed |
|---|---|---|---|
| cargo-build.log | `cargo build` (serde, serde_json) | 198 | 198 |
| git-clone-progress.log | `git clone --progress psf/requests` | 2,101 | 220 |
| npm-install-verbose.log | `npm install express --loglevel=verbose` | 2,744 | 1,142 |
| pip-install-verbose.log | `pip install -v httpx rich` | 1,159 | 1,158 |
| pytest-verbose-failing.log | `pytest -v` with 60 passing and 3 failing tests | 1,814 | 661 |
| pytest-verbose-passing.log | `pytest -v -rA` on this repo | 884 | 884 |
| **total** | | **8,900** | **4,263 (−52.1%)** |

All 12 `FAILED`/`assert`/`KeyError` lines of the failing pytest log survive compression.
The corpus is small. Please contribute more real logs.

## Snapshots

`keelyard bench` snapshots into a temporary shadow repo (your timeline is untouched). *Warm*: one file edited, snapshot. *Cold*: the index is dropped first. Five runs each, Linux box, Oct 2026.

| Repo | Tracked files | First snapshot | Warm median | Cold median |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| keelyard | 112 | 174 ms | 8 ms | 24 ms |
| django (shallow clone) | 7,083 | 2.34 s | 88 ms | 427 ms |

Only files changed since the last snapshot are size-checked, so warm cost tracks the edit, not the repo.

## Arena, local run

`examples/arena/discount`, five hidden checks, qwen-coder 1.5B on Ollama: do nothing 0/5, one-shot qwen 0/5 (226 in / 63 out tokens), reference fix 5/5. No Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode runs yet.

## Feature matrix

`python bench/feature_matrix.py` runs every CLI command and flag, every hook and every MCP tool; results in [feature-matrix.md](feature-matrix.md).

## Swarm with a small local model

These are real calls to `qwen2.5-coder-1.5b-instruct` (Q4_K_M GGUF) served by Ollama on CPU, with concurrency 4.
There were 12 tasks against this repo: 8 Q&A or summaries, 2 patch drafts and 2 greps.

- Wall time: 4 min 15 s; helper tokens: 14,452 in, 1,409 out.
- Verified: 3/12. Both greps are local and need no model. One patch passed `git apply --check`; the other did not apply.
- Q&A: 0/8 answers contained a valid `path:line` citation, and the verifier marked all 8 UNVERIFIED.
  A second run with a format example in the prompt also verified 0/8. One answer copied the example's
  file name, so the example was removed again.

Conclusion: the verification layer does its job, but a 1.5B model is not a useful helper. Use a 7B+ local model or
a hosted cheap model. We have not yet measured how well larger models verify.

## Not yet measured

- `reads`: repeated identical reads in real Claude Code transcripts (harness exists, no transcripts on the build box).
- `memory`: recall@8 and snippet/transcript ratio on real sessions (harness exists, same reason).

## Swarm quality

`python bench/swarm_quality.py --runs 2`, local qwen-coder 1.5B on Ollama, 2026-10-12. Five one-function bug
fixes and five "which line does X" questions, in a repo where each file also carries 25 unrelated helpers.
*Single* is the old swarm: whole file, one sample, diff output, `git apply --check` only. *Pipeline* is the
new one: context pack, one-definition rewrite, tests on a copy, best-of-3, one retry with feedback, no
escalation (no strong model configured). Ground truth for fixes is that module's own tests passing with the
patch; for questions, citing the expected line.

| | single, run 1 / 2 | pipeline, run 1 / 2 |
|---|---|---|
| fixes actually correct | 0 / 0 of 5 | 4 / 4 of 5 |
| fixes marked verified but wrong | 3 / 2 | 0 / 0 |
| questions citing the right line | 1 / 1 of 5 | 2 / 3 of 5 |
| questions marked verified | 1 / 1 | 5 / 5 |
| model calls | 10 / 10 | 33 / 39 |
| input tokens | 12,435 / 12,435 | 5,034 / 6,309 |
| output tokens | 1,679 / 1,712 | 2,835 / 3,626 |

Checking patches against tests removed every false "verified" fix, and the rewrite format plus retries took a
1.5B model from 0 to 4 correct fixes out of 5. Context packs used about half the input tokens despite 3-4x
more calls. What it does not show: a "verified" answer to a question means its citations exist, not that it is
right (5 verified, 2-3 right). Ten tasks on one tiny model is a smoke test, not a benchmark; escalation and
7B+ models are not measured here.


### Cooperative swarm vs the best local setup

Same 10 tasks (5 bug fixes, 5 questions), qwen-coder-1.5b on Ollama, 2 runs each. `python bench/swarm_quality.py`.

| mode | correct of 20 (2 runs × 10) | tokens | tokens per correct | wrong patches marked verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| single | 2 | 27,394 | 13,697 | 5 |
| pipeline | 15 | 19,073 | 1,272 | 0 |
| best-local | 18 | 28,081 | 1,560 | 0 |
| coop-nocritic | 15 | 19,686 | 1,312 | 0 |
| coop | 15 | 44,149 | 2,943 | 0 |

- `best-local` is the same model with more samples and retries (best_of 5, retries 2). It stands in for "one
  strong agent" because no stronger model or API key was available. That comparison is still open.
- `coop` adds the critic. It doubled the tokens and did not improve quality, so `critic` is off by default.
- `coop-nocritic` (blackboard, voting, budget) costs about the same as the pipeline per correct answer.
  With one model the ladder had one step, so routing was not exercised here (it is covered by tests).

### Free OpenRouter helper (one run)

Same 10 tasks with `cohere/north-mini-code:free` as the helper, cost $0:

| mode | correct of 10 | tokens | tokens per correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| single | 6 | 13,699 | 2,283 |
| pipeline | 10 | 8,504 | 850 |
| coop-nocritic | 10 | 12,915 | 1,292 |

One run only: the free tier allows 50 requests a day and the limit was reached during the strong-model modes
(`nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free`), so there is no strong-model comparison yet. `bench/swarm_openrouter_free.json`.

## keelyard's own overhead

`python bench/overhead.py` counts what keelyard adds to every session (characters / 4 of compact JSON or text):

| item | tokens |
|---|---|
| MCP tool schemas, 13 core tools (default) | 1,582 |
| MCP tool schemas, all 22 tools (`[mcp] tools = "all"`) | 2,401 |
| MCP server instructions | 77 |
| CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md guide block | 144 |
| session brief, fresh project (cap 600) | 74 |
| **total per session, fresh project** | **1,877** |
| workflow guide, only when asked (plan / debug / review) | 240 / 181 / 182 |

Prompt recall adds at most 250 tokens per prompt and only when past sessions match; hints are capped at 12 per session.

Net: the 8 filtered commands above saved 50,621 tokens, so one session that runs them nets
**48,744** tokens. At the median saving per command, the fixed overhead is repaid after
4 filtered commands. A session that never runs a noisy command pays the 1,877 tokens and saves nothing;
these are per-command measurements, not totals from real sessions.

# Landscape

Tools people use to make coding agents cheaper or more reliable, and what keelyard took from them.
"Measured" means we ran it; everything else is the project's own claim or a description, not our number.
Stars and licenses from GitHub, October 2026.

| project | stars | license | technique | effect | in keelyard |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rtk | 83k | Apache-2.0 | per-command output filters | measured: 56,522 → 5,747 tokens on our 8 commands (keelyard: 5,901) | `run`, `filter`, `run_compact` (own code) |
| repomix | 28.8k | MIT | pack repo, compress to structure | claimed large reductions; not measured | `code outline`, `project_map` |
| aider | 49.5k | Apache-2.0 | ranked repo map | described; not measured | `project_map`, swarm context packs |
| serena | 30k | see repo | symbol-level find/edit over LSP | described; not measured | `find_symbol`, `read_file` ranges |
| context7 | 63k | MIT | fetch current library docs on demand | described; not measured | not adopted (network service, off-mission) |
| code2prompt | 7.7k | MIT | repo to prompt with templates | described | not adopted (overlaps repomix idea) |
| LLMLingua | 6.8k | MIT | model-based prompt compression | paper claims up to 20x | not adopted (needs a model at runtime) |
| caveman | 111.8k | Apache-2.0 | terse-reply rule | claimed output savings; not measured | one "Be terse" rule |
| claude-context | 12.6k | MIT | vector code search via MCP | described | not adopted (needs embedding service) |
| ccusage | 19k | see repo | usage from local logs | n/a | `usage` (own code) |
| superpowers | 299k | MIT | skills: plan, debug, review workflows | n/a | workflow pack, lazy (240/181/182 tokens on demand) |
| spec-kit | 141k | MIT | spec → plan → tasks | n/a | `proof add` requirements + plan workflow |
| claude-task-master | 28k | see repo | task lists for agents | n/a | covered by proof requirements |
| claude-code-router | 37.7k | MIT | route requests to cheaper models | n/a | `route_task`, swarm escalation |
| playwright-mcp | 38k | Apache-2.0 | browser control for agents | n/a | `proof_screenshot` (optional extra) |

## MCP tools

Called over stdio by the official MCP client. Error rows check that bad input is refused.

| | tool | arguments | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| ✓ | `status` | `{}` | ok |
